newsitem.title: USA: US budget plan funds disputed forest, mine buyouts.
newsitem.headline: US budget plan funds disputed forest, mine buyouts.

text.p: The fiscal 1998 budget plan pending in Congress provides funds to buy the Headwaters Forest in northern California and the New World mine near Yellowstone National Park, lawmakers and a White House official said Tuesday.

"Together with the congressional leadership, we plan to work with the Budget and Appropriations committees to achieve these goals," Kathleen McGinty, chair of the Council on Environmental Quality, told a House Resources subcommittee.
In both cases, the Clinton administration agreed to acquire the properties in the name of environmental protection.

Purchase of the Headwaters Forest in Humboldt County, California, would preserve 3,425 acres (1,386 hectares) of virgin redwoods owned by MAXXAM Inc. Under a pact reached last fall, MAXXAM would receive money from the federal and state governments as well as $80 million worth of state and federal forest land.
In the "buyout" of the New World gold, copper and silver mine, Crown Butte Mines Inc would receive $65 million ln federal funds.
McGinty said the budget reserved $700 million in a land and water conservation fund for high-priority transactions.
"The administration's top priorities are New World mine and Headwaters Forest proposals," McGinty said.
She said $315 million had been set aside for the two transactions. Use of the rest of the funds would be negotiated between Congress and the administration, she said.

Wyoming Republican Barbara Cubin, who heads the mineral resources subcommittee, also described the budget plan in the same general terms. The administration originally proposed to offset cost of the Crown Butte deal by delaying for one year the entry of some land into the Conservation Reserve. Farm-state lawmakers strongly opposed that idea.

Under questioning from Cubin, McGinty said there were no plans to use the land and water conservation fund to buy oil and gas rights near the Everglades in South Florida or to buy land in the newly formed Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument.
